concepts.title: Suraj and the Dragon of His Dreams
concepts.section: The Tunnel, Let us read I
concepts.definition: Suraj, a boy from town, cycles to a jungle cutting to watch the noon train burst from the tunnel like a beautiful monster; his longing to know the inside of the tunnel leads him to the watchman's hut and a night friendship.
concepts.key_idea: Curiosity turns a railway cutting into an adventure; the steam engine is imagined as a dragon out of Suraj's dreams.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr104.txt, The Tunnel, Let us read I

solution_steps.explain: Retell what happens in one or two sentences with the main character named.

concepts.title: Sunder Singh: The Watchman with the Lamp
concepts.definition: Sunder Singh guards the tunnel for years, inspecting it morning and night and warning the engine driver with a flag or lamp; his hut, marigolds and leopard stories make him the wise, lonely heart of the jungle.
concepts.key_idea: Duty done with love turns a small job into guardianship of train, leopard and jungle alike.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr104.txt, The Tunnel, Let us read

concepts.title: Saving the Leopard from the Night Mail
concepts.section: The Tunnel, Let us read II
concepts.definition: Hearing the leopard's sawing call inside the tunnel, Sunder Singh and Suraj walk into the dark with an axe and a lamp and shout it clear of the tracks before the night mail arrives, so that neither animal nor train is harmed.
concepts.key_idea: Real courage protects: two friends face snarling darkness to save a wild animal they have never tamed.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr104.txt, The Tunnel, Let us read II

solution_steps.explain: Note the sound that tells the leopard is crouching between the tracks.

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Embankment, Contemplation and Sinewy
concepts.definition: The story's glossary builds the jungle scene: a railway embankment carries the line over low ground, contemplation is deep thought, sinewy means lean and muscular, and dazzling light blinds the eyes.
concepts.key_idea: Precise words like shimmered, scuttled and snarling let the reader hear and feel the cutting.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr104.txt, The Tunnel, Let us learn

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does Sunder Singh refuse to let the night mail be stopped for a porcupine but act at once for the leopard?

solution_template.explain: Small animals on the line are not worth halting a train; he stops only for real danger to it.
A big animal would be killed and might derail the train, so he drives it out himself instead.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How did Suraj know the train was about to come out of the tunnel?

solution_template.explain: He heard the shrill whistle of the engine in the distance.
A rumble like distant thunder issued from the tunnel just before the engine shot out.
